note: Individual airframes (future liveries) and the variant each attaches to by default. default_variant is data: change it here when better evidence appears. 'known' features are documented for that airframe; 'inferred' come from its build date and production ranges.

sources.ijn-tail-photo: IJN photo of the T1-323 wreck tail, 1943-44: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Yamamoto%27s_airplane_crash.jpg (Agawa, The Reluctant Admiral, p. 204) and https://pacificwrecks.com/aircraft/g4m/2656/1943/yamamoto-shrine-tail-323.html
sources.model-art-2012: Model Art, April 2012 (歴史群像 太平洋戦史 Vol.42 p.32; 丸メカニック No.22 p.72), as cited at https://beebee.air-nifty.com/momo/2021/06/post-d87b0f.html
sources.ja-wikipedia-g4m: JA Wikipedia 一式陸上攻撃機: Kasei 15 from the 406th aircraft (Aug 1942), citing JACAR C12070526100
sources.en-wikipedia-g4m: EN Wikipedia Mitsubishi G4M (secondary): propeller spinners from summer 1942; cut-away tail cone from spring 1943; redesigned V-cut cone from August 1943
sources.coles-1968-panels: Cole's aircraft blog, Yamamoto's aircraft wreck history (1968 panels) http://colesaircraft.blogspot.com/2015/03/yamamotos-aircraft-wreck-history-art.html
sources.ja-wikipedia-incident: JA Wikipedia 海軍甲事件 https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/海軍甲事件
sources.awm-rel01198: Australian War Memorial REL/01198 control horn https://www.awm.gov.au/collection/C114448
sources.j-aircraft-colours: j-aircraft IJNAF colours FAQ (general 1944 standard, not airframe-specific) https://j-aircraft.com/faq/IJNAF_Colors.htm

airframes.event: Shot down over Bougainville 18 April 1943 carrying Admiral Yamamoto

built.value: about March 1943, Mitsubishi No. 3 Works, Nagoya

airframes.default_variant_basis: INFERRED from the build date: Kasei 15 from airframe No. 406 (Aug 1942); no record of this airframe's engine mark was found

known.value: 323 on the fin, light digits from the fin leading edge; no room for a T1- prefix on that side
known.basis: B&W photo: white consistent, yellow not excluded

known.value: thin white circular outline on green, black 'Lift Here' stencil

unresolved.basis: built at the spring-1943 change; the wreck shows bare frame
conflicting: grey over red primer on 1968 panels, bare duralumin (歴史群像 Vol.42), grey (Pacific Wrecks, unsourced)
705 Ku used T1 from about March 1943 (Arawasi) or June 1943 (EN Wikipedia)

unit_note.value: Misawa Kokutai renamed 705 Kokutai on 1 Nov 1942; at Vunakanau, Rabaul

crew.note: readings differ between sources; names as in the Japanese sources

members.name: 飛行兵曹長 小谷立 (Kotani; given name read Takeo or Takashi)
大崎明春 (also given as 大崎朋春)
畑信雄 (Hata; Pacific Wrecks has Hara)
上田春雄 (kitabatake: 山田春雄)

crew.fate: all 11 killed; crashed inland of Moila Point near Aku, 06°47.165′S 155°33.137′E

markings_evidence.item: upper surfaces green, lower grey, black upper nose and cowlings, yellow inner-wing leading-edge strip

ranking: light grey over iron-oxide red primer on panels removed in 1968, aotake inside (coles-1968-panels; underside attribution is the seller's)
bare duralumin from the factory (歴史群像 Vol.42 p.32), bare then grey or silver (丸メカニック No.22 p.72), both via model-art-2012
red primer visible on a 1970s postcard, location unspecified (https://pacificwrecks.com/aircraft/g4m/2656/1970s/postcard-yamamoto-wreckage-front.html)

markings_evidence.item: IJN colour standard names (D1 upper, J3 lower) are the general 1944 standard

surviving_parts.part: left outer wing panel and the admiral's seat

surviving_parts.where: PNG National Museum per EN Wikipedia; unknown per Pacific Wrecks

photos.note: cited by URL only; no image is stored in the package

airframes.event: Shot down 18 April 1943 carrying Vice Admiral Ugaki; ditched off Moila Point

built.note: construction number unknown; Pacific Wrecks rejects 2659 for lack of a primary source

airframes.default_variant_basis: INFERRED: same unit and date as T1-323, presumed of the same production period; no record of the airframe

unresolved.basis: no photo or wreck evidence; Pacific Wrecks' marking text repeats T1-323's

members.name: Fujimoto Fumikatsu, Itō Sukeichi, Hachiki Isamu, Nomiyama Kaneyoshi, Kuriyama Nobuyuki

passengers.name: Imanaka Kaoru, Muroi Sutej[i], Tomono Rinji

crew.fate: ditched about 100 m off Moila Point about 08:00; a 2018 side-scan sonar search found nothing
